circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, this 5. 281-kilometer circuit designed by Hermann Tilke has served as the venue for the season-concluding Formula One Grand Prix since 2009. The track ranks as the second Middle Eastern Formula One facility, following Bahrain's earlier debut and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the Formula One Australian Grand Prix every year alongside various supporting racing categories. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status, meeting the highest international standards for motorsport facilities.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit originally operated as the Österreichring and held the Austrian Grand Prix annually from 1970 through 1987. After undergoing redesign and shortening, the track was renamed and resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street venue in Azerbaijan's capital, spanning 6. 003 km and ranking as the fourth-longest Formula One track. The circuit first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016 before transitioning to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting in 2017.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: The Bahrain International Circuit, inaugurated in 2004, stretches 5. 412 kilometers and holds FIA Grade 1 status. It hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One grand prix that year and continues to stage the annual race, alongside hosting drag racing, open-wheel series events, and endurance competitions.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya near Barcelona spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of lengthy straights and diverse cornering sections, making it a versatile test for racing machinery. Holding an FIA Grade 1 license, the facility accommodates over 140,000 spectators across its grandstand infrastructure.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The Belgian circuit sprawls across 7. 004 kilometres through the Ardennes region near Stavelot, hosting one of Formula One's most prestigious events. Since debuting as a Grand Prix venue in 1925 and featuring in the sport's inaugural 1950 season, the track has maintained near-continuous presence on the F1 calendar since 1985, with only two gaps in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, this 4. 361 km circuit serves as the home of the Canadian Grand Prix in Formula One. Beyond its role in F1, the venue has accommodated various other major racing series including sportscar championships, open-wheel competitions, and NASCAR events throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit is a motorsport venue primarily recognized for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which has been held there periodically since 2004 with a return to the calendar from 2024 onward. The track has recently expanded its racing calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix, beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near villages in Northamptonshire, Silverstone hosted the inaugural World Championship Grand Prix in 1950 and has served as the primary home of the British Grand Prix since permanently establishing itself as the venue in 1987, having previously shared hosting duties with two other circuits. The track remains a significant racing venue, accommodating multiple motorsport series beyond Formula One.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km circuit in Mogyoród near Budapest, hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held in a Soviet-bloc nation when it debuted in 1986. Built in just eight months on land near a major highway after government officials rejected plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park, the venue was constructed as a memorial to János Drapál, Hungary's pioneering motorcycle racer.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922, making it the third purpose-built racing facility globally and Europe's oldest on the mainland. The track, renowned as the "Temple of Speed" for its extended straights and rapid corners, has hosted the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949, except for 1980, and remains one of only four venues featured continuously throughout Formula One's history.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan, is a 5. 807 km motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland with a spectator capacity of 155,000. The track is renowned for hosting major Formula One races and Japanese Super Formula championships.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that winds through Paradise, Nevada, incorporating famous landmarks such as the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas. The track follows Las Vegas Boulevard and the surrounding urban streets, taking advantage of the iconic casino and hotel district that defines the city's character.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit named in honor of two Mexican racing brothers who both perished in accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix across multiple eras, returning to the calendar in 2015 on its current layout after a 23-year absence, with the race now officially designated the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners that allows qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, the venue joined the championship calendar in 2022 and primarily hosts the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street course that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, following the harbour's perimeter in Monaco. It is typically known as "Monte Carlo" due to its substantial portion running through the Monte Carlo area.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the coastal dunes near Amsterdam in the Netherlands, this 4. 259 km circuit made a triumphant return to Formula One in 2021 when it hosted the revived Dutch Grand Prix. The venue's involvement with the championship concluded in 2026, ending a brief but significant presence on the modern racing calendar.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Lusail International Circuit, situated near Doha in Qatar, spans 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight and holds an FIA Grade 1 license.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing circuit in São Paulo, inaugurated in 1940 and renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace. The counterclockwise layout hosts the Brazilian Grand Prix and features an adjacent kart facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a Saudi Arabian street track situated along the Red Sea waterfront that has been home to the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural 2021 edition. The venue also began hosting a Formula E race in 2025, establishing itself as a multi-category motorsport destination.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a street-based racing venue located around Marina Bay in Singapore, spanning the Downtown Core and Kallang districts.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit offers a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse cornering sequences that test multiple racing disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates over 140,000 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located near Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that hosts multiple racing series, most notably Formula One's United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the venue accommodates NASCAR events, MotoGP's Motorcycle Grand Prix of the Americas, and various endurance racing championships, establishing itself as a significant motorsport destination in North America.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a dual Thai and British racing driver who represents Thailand in Formula One, currently driving for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships in 2005 and 2006 with Renault while amassing 32 Grand Prix victories over 23 seasons. Beyond his single-seater success, Alonso has achieved remarkable feats in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the only driver to win both the Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Antonelli is an Italian Formula One driver racing for Mercedes who has claimed eight Grand Prix victories following his 2025 debut.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One as a member of the Audi team. Known for his competitive performances, he has established himself as a professional competitor at the sport's highest level.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas is a Finnish Formula One driver currently racing for Cadillac. The 13-season veteran has claimed 10 Grand Prix victories and finished as championship runner-up twice during his Mercedes tenure, in both 2019 and 2020.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently competing in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan holds a reserve role with Haas while primarily competing in European endurance racing with Nielsen Racing in the LMP2 category. Between 2024 and 2025, he made seven Formula One race appearances.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently competing for Alpine. He achieved a notable victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while driving for AlphaTauri earlier in his career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar represents France in Formula One racing, competing for Red Bull Racing. He holds dual French and Algerian nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who shares the record for most world championship titles with seven victories, equaling Michael Schumacher's achievement. He also holds multiple records including the highest number of race wins, pole positions, and podium appearances in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One and has achieved considerable success in other motorsport disciplines, including a victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans with Porsche in 2015.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver competes for Ferrari in Formula One, where he has secured nine race victories throughout his nine seasons in the sport. Leclerc finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while driving for the Italian team.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen, a Danish racing driver, competed in Formula One across two separate periods from 2014 to 2020 and again from 2022 to 2024. Currently, he races in the FIA World Endurance Championship as a factory driver for BMW with WRT, while also pursuing a part-time NASCAR career with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver competing for McLaren, claimed the Formula One World Drivers' Championship in 2025. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The veteran competitor secured a Grand Prix victory in 2021 during his tenure with Alpine, specifically at the Hungarian circuit.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez, known as "Checo," finished second in the 2023 Formula One drivers' championship while racing for Red Bull and has claimed six race victories throughout his 15 seasons in the sport. He currently competes for Cadillac in Formula One.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, where he has accumulated nine Grand Prix victories since joining the grid.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: An Australian driver who raced in Formula One between 2011 and 2024, Ricciardo earned eight Grand Prix victories throughout his 14-season career. Known by the moniker "the Honey Badger," he competed at the sport's highest level for over a decade before retiring from the championship.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell has secured seven Grand Prix victories during his eight-season Formula One career and currently races for Mercedes.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, having secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-year career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition. He previously spent two seasons in Formula One between 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sportcar racing.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Canadian driver Lance Stroll currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, competing at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese racing driver, holds reserve driver positions with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. He competed as a full-time driver from 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: A Dutch-Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing, Verstappen has secured four consecutive Formula One World Drivers' Championship titles between 2021 and 2024 while accumulating 71 Grand Prix victories over his 12-season career.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is China's sole Formula One competitor, having raced in the sport between 2022 and 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. He currently holds the position of backup driver for the American team while maintaining his status as the only Chinese-origin driver to participate in Formula One competition.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Operating from its Enstone base since 2021, Alpine has served as Renault's official Formula One works team under various sponsorship arrangements. The squad, previously known as Renault F1 Team, was rebranded to showcase Renault's Alpine sports car marque and maintained this connection until the manufacturer's departure from the sport at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has maintained a presence in Formula One through different organizational structures, with its contemporary iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, having participated in every World Championship season since the sport's inception in 1950. The squad's iconic identity centers on the Prancing Horse emblem, which has become synonymous with the sport's most storied outfit.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: The TGR Haas F1 Team is an American-licensed outfit founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas in 2014, competing in Formula One since the 2016 season. Ayao Komatsu currently leads the team as principal, taking over from Guenther Steiner, who held the position from the team's establishment through early 2024.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering and racing enterprise established by Peter Sauber in 1970, the company distinguished itself through endurance racing success including a Le Mans victory before joining Formula One in 1993. Following numerous operational changes across three decades, the team competed until 2025 as one of the championship's longest-running constructors before being purchased by Audi to serve as the foundation for its factory team entry.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that operates as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group. The team is currently owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company and competes in the sport under its corporate sponsorship banner.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954, operating as both a constructor and engine supplier across multiple eras. The modern Mercedes-AMG Petronas team, based in Brackley and licensed under Germany, became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Toto Wolff, and Ineos from January 2022, with the outfit historically known as the "Silver Arrows.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull's two-team operation. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the team operates alongside Red Bull Racing under Austrian conglomerate Red Bull GmbH's ownership structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor competing since 2024, based in Faenza with a secondary facility near its sister team in Milton Keynes. As one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned constructors alongside Red Bull Racing, the team represents the energy drink company's second competitive entry in the sport.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, established in 2005 under an Austrian licence, operates as one of two Formula One teams owned by Red Bull GmbH and is headquartered in England. The team was led by Christian Horner throughout its existence until his departure in 2025, with Laurent Mekies assuming the leadership role. Racing Bulls serves as the conglomerate's sister team in the championship.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, is a British Formula One constructor currently competing as Atlassian Williams F1 Team. The team emerged following the collapse of Williams's previous F1 venture and maintains its headquarters at a major facility in Grove, Oxfordshire.
